methods.name: LOOK FOR YOUR NUMBERS SOMEWHERE ELSE
methods.result: Reconciled the scalar path law with classical Ehrenfest/Krawtchouk and Davies/Combes-Thomas machinery and proved a self-adjoint finite-band degree-distance semigroup gate: ||Pi_<=D exp(-tA) Pi_>=K|| <= exp[-s(K-D)-(kappa-beta cosh(sw))t] when beta cosh(sw)<kappa.

methods.name: PROVE SOMETHING WEAKER, COMPLETELY
methods.result: Translated Chen-Li arXiv:2608.06279 into the pressure framework: their vanishing-LDA plus low-interface/treewidth hypotheses imply chi2(q_*) -> 0 for every fixed q_*<1, hence Psi(q_*)=0 and q_c=1. This is known in substance from Chen-Li and remains a restricted PARTIAL class relative to the source.

methods.name: DO ONE SCALE, ONE DIRECTION AT A TIME
methods.result: Proved a central-band orbit-collision theorem: for a symmetrized binary linear code of dimension k in E coordinates, at retention q the collision contribution from weights |j-qE/(1+q)| <= sqrt((k+2)ln2 E/2) is at least 4^{-(k+1)}(1+q)^E. For Mao, pressure is therefore localized at j=(q/(1+q)+o(1))E >> D_n.

new_results: Reversible exponential source-degree distance gate under diagonal coercivity, symmetric transition budget, and finite degree bandwidth.
Explicit pressure bridge q_c=1 for the Chen-Li low-interface/treewidth positive class under their vanishing low-degree premise.
MacWilliams/Hoeffding/Cauchy central-band localization of symmetrized code collision pressure; Mao's fixed-noise pressure lies near the binomial tilt degree qE/(1+q).
prior_art_cautions: Ehrenfest/Krawtchouk birth-death spectral theory is classical.
Davies exponential conjugation and Combes-Thomas/block-Jacobi off-diagonal methods are classical.
Chen-Li's planted-subgraph positive theorem is prior art; only its pressure-language bridge is recorded here.
MacWilliams/Delsarte identities, Reed-Muller weight-distribution/list-decoding theory, binomial large deviations, and group averaging are classical.
Bounded negative search is not novelty proof; inference-specific novelty remains UNVERIFIED.
